claims.text: Adding 5–10 wt% Ni to TiB2-based components will significantly improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion relative to undoped TiB2.
Undoped powder-metallurgy TiB2 has grain boundaries vulnerable to penetration by molten aluminum.
The proposed intervention is incorporation of 5–10 wt% Ni into a TiB2 matrix during powder-metallurgy processing.
The proposed processing includes sintering at 1400–1500 °C under a reducing atmosphere.
The specified Ni addition and sintering treatment will produce Ni-bearing intermetallic phases.
The Ni-bearing intermetallic phases will preferentially localize along TiB2 grain boundaries.
Ni doping alters interfacial thermodynamic equilibrium and reaction pathways in the TiB2–molten-aluminum system.
Ni-rich grain-boundary phases reduce the chemical potential for aluminum dissolution.
Stable secondary phases can impede corrosion by a molten material by forming a blocking reaction layer.
Ni-bearing grain-boundary phases will act as physical barriers to molten-aluminum infiltration.
Blocking molten-aluminum infiltration at grain boundaries will decelerate corrosion.
Ni-doped TiB2 will exhibit slower degradation than undoped TiB2 over equivalent exposure times.
Ni-doped TiB2 will exhibit less intergranular penetration by molten aluminum than undoped TiB2.
Ni-doped TiB2 will retain better microstructural integrity than undoped TiB2.
Conventional undoped TiB2 undergoes relatively rapid grain-boundary corrosion in molten aluminum under the stated service conditions.
The corrosion benefit depends on the Ni-bearing phases remaining stable during prolonged exposure to molten aluminum at approximately 660 °C.
The corrosion benefit depends on tightly controlling sintering temperature and atmosphere so that the targeted grain-boundary microstructure forms.
